- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp declines, model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after recent spikes (e.g., 70+), especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — add a small upward bias to correct for mean reversion.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >5% gap) and sentiment is positive, consider lagged momentum — forecast may be too conservative; add 1–2% upward adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period price surges (last 5–7 days of true outcome) — apply a “late-period correction” by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is positive and recent price is rising.
- If sentiment is high but model shows a sharp drop in forecast mid-period, check for “sentiment reversal” — may indicate overreaction; adjust downward slightly to avoid overcorrection.
